not-supported.md §DESTROY called by garbage collector — t23 is the ONLY failing row (22/1 vs perl 23/0): after `delete $_[0]` in a sub, the blessed arg's DESTROY must fire when the enclosing block drops the last reference. Probe s319: PCL agrees on t21/t22 (flag stays 0 inside f and after f) and only misses the scope-exit DESTROY — refcount-deterministic destruction, which PCL does not have.

not-supported.md §Unicode semantics differences — t6 is the ONLY failing row (5/1 vs perl 6/0): `crypt` writing to a utf8 target must turn the target's UTF-8 flag OFF. Probe s319: PCL's crypt VALUE is correct (t5 passes); only `utf8::is_utf8($x)` differs, because PCL has no per-scalar UTF-8 flag (CL strings are always Unicode).

not-supported.md §Error compatibility for invalid Perl input (CLAUDE.md §9, verbatim example) — ALL 274 failing rows (1476/274 vs perl 1750/0) are the SAME assertion: `is eval("sub { \$a <=> \$b <=> \$c }"), undef, "… non-associative"`, i.e. invalid Perl must FAIL TO COMPILE. PCL is a transpiler for working Perl, not a validator, so it compiles the chain and returns a coderef (probe s319). Counted every row: 274 of 274 say "non-associative", none assert a value. The legitimately CHAINABLE comparisons (`$a == $b == $c`) work correctly in PCL — verified — so this is exclusively the rejection category, task #149 :principle9.

not-supported.md §Unicode semantics differences — t3 is the ONLY failing row (2/1 vs perl 3/0): reading MALFORMED (overlong) UTF-8 through a `<:utf8` in-memory handle and printing it must pass the bytes through unchanged. Probe s319: PCL emits c3 81 c2 af … where perl emits c1 af …, i.e. it holds the scalar as CHARACTERS and re-encodes on output — no per-scalar UTF-8/byte flag (CL strings are always Unicode). NB the open itself was ALSO broken until s319 (task #171, `<:utf8` was rejected outright); this row is what remains after that fix.

not-supported.md §Error compatibility for invalid Perl input (CLAUDE.md §9) — t19 is the ONLY failing row (19/1 vs perl 19/0): `eval 'exists &t5()'` must set $@ =~ /not a subroutine name/. PCL DOES reject the invalid form — probe s319 gives "invalid number of arguments: 1" — so only the MESSAGE TEXT differs, and exact fatal-error text is not a goal (user 2026-07-28). Task #149 category :principle9.

not-supported.md §Unicode semantics differences — ALL 7 failing rows (38/7 vs perl 45/0) are two blessed subsections. t10-13 are the `### use bytes` block (t/op/chr.t lines 28-31: under the pragma `chr(-1)` must be the single byte "\xFF"; PCL has no byte view, so it keeps "\x{FFFD}"). t40-42 are `### Code points above U+10FFFF` (lines 80-82: chr(0x110000)/0x1FFFFF/0x200000 in perl's extended UTF-8) — measured s319/s320: SBCL's char-code-limit is 1114112, so a CL string physically cannot hold them and (code-char #x110000) yields no character. Blessed in fable-answers-s318.md §11; task #173.

not-supported.md §Error compatibility for invalid Perl input (CLAUDE.md §9) + §DESTROY called by garbage collector — ALL 7 failing rows (66/7 vs perl 71/0) are two blessed categories, established row-by-row s321 after the TAP re-alignment (task #177) showed the old number-join had blamed two rows that PASS. (a) perl t63-t66 + PCL's 2 EXTRA rows: one `foreach my $mode (qw(subname("arg") subname() $subref("arg") $subref()))` loop asserting `$@ =~ /\Asyntax error/`. `do SUBNAME(LIST)` was VALID Perl before 5.20 and meant call-the-sub; PCL keeps that historical semantics, so the assertions fail AND each test's `fail()` guard fires (those are the 2 PCL-only rows — the same divergence, not a second defect). Ruled no-fix in fable-answers-s318.md §4, task #158 :principle9. (b) perl t68 "RT 124248": `f(do { 1; !!(my $x = bless []) })` requires the blessed temp to be DESTROYed at do-block exit (FREETMPS) before f() runs — refcount-deterministic destruction, which PCL does not have; same family as op/args.t t23. NB t67 (delete-helem copied) and t70 ($@ false on do dir) PASS — probed s321 — and t71 ($! is EISDIR on do dir) was FIXED s321 (p-do now carries the OS errno into $!).
